source_review.notes: Checked current official records for ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288:2023 and 42010:2022; ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 current-confirmation information; the official INCOSE Handbook fifth-edition record; NASA/SP-2016-6105 Rev 2; NIST SP 800-160 Vol. 1 Rev. 1; and the current SEBoK. Standards, guidance and living-reference status are distinguished, and none is treated as proof that a particular boundary is adequate.

evidence: Checked bounded-context tuple C_(c,l,v)=(S,E,B,I,A,K,O) and definitions for concern, lifecycle stage and viewpoint.
Checked modeled universe U, system set S subset U, relevant environment E subset of U minus S, and directed crossing relation I subset of (SxE) union (ExS).
Checked membership function B_(c,l,v)(x) and operational, development, business/mission, system context and architecture-description distinctions.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Set notation is an analytical aid and does not imply that sociotechnical membership is naturally binary or permanent.

Confirmed three crossings contain owner, contract, assumption and mode and two are incomplete.

numerical_recomputation.notes: Counts establish only completeness against four synthetic metadata fields.

evidence: Traced every listed crossing as internal-to-external or external-to-internal relative to the declared membership map.
Checked the closure invariant requires material dependencies and consequences to be governed inside or represented at the boundary.
Checked claim-scope reasoning from component evidence through operational and enabling-system context.
Checked multiple concern boundaries are related models rather than mutually exclusive universal classifications.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Structural membership and relation expressions cannot establish relevance, legitimacy, behavior or outcome.

evidence: Reviewed empty and universe-wide boundaries, narrow product versus broad capability scope, nested systems, overlapping concern boundaries and independently governed systems of systems.
Reviewed people, procedures, suppliers, regulation, natural environment, market, infrastructure, data, adversaries and affected communities as possible elements or context.
Reviewed development, deployment, normal, peak, degraded, emergency, maintenance, attack, recovery, evolution and retirement conditions.

boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Jurisdiction-specific authority, public acceptance and high-stakes operational adequacy remain named human-review obligations.

evidence: Checked every boundary requires purpose, concern, scope, lifecycle stage, viewpoint, owner and revision trigger.
Checked material crossings require direction, semantics, timing, quality, failure behavior and authority proportional to risk.
Checked external does not mean irrelevant and internal does not imply control.
Checked assumptions require owners, evidence, monitoring or review triggers and consequences if false.
Checked no-displaced-harm reasoning covers downstream, operator, privacy, maintenance, waste and retirement consequences.
invariant_checking.notes: The executable inventory enforces only authority and four crossing metadata fields, not the full prose invariant set.

evidence: Reviewed boundary adequacy as a falsifiable engineering argument rather than a theorem or discovered fact.
Reviewed counterexamples where contract, organization, physical enclosure, security authorization and operational boundaries diverge.
Reviewed why a component test, schema, standard diagram, supplier ownership or laboratory result cannot prove whole-system outcome.
Confirmed successful structural checking is never presented as proof of stakeholder value, safety, legality, security or operational success.
proof_review.notes: The module supplies conditional arguments and counterexamples, not formal verification of a sociotechnical system.

evidence: Audited uses of system, boundary, complete, adequate, closure, prove, authority, control, safe, secure, lawful and acceptance.
Each adequacy claim is scoped to concern, lifecycle stage, viewpoint and evidence; standards and structured models are not treated as substantive assurance.
No external academic, practitioner, safety, regulatory, community or operational review is claimed.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: High-consequence approval is explicitly reserved for named authorized reviewers and real system evidence.

Reproduced entities=6, crossings=5, complete_crossings=3 and the exact five sorted findings under the recorded Python 3 toolchain.

empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Execution demonstrates one declared consistency policy over a synthetic inventory only.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter defines system and system-of-interest boundaries as purpose-, concern-, lifecycle- and viewpoint-dependent engineering choices; integrates environments, external entities, interfaces and enabling systems; and preserves later modules' ownership of purpose, stakeholders, emergence, scenarios, requirements and architecture depth.

practitioner_review.notes: Practice guidance covers inclusion/exclusion rules, multiple related boundaries, context inventories, interface semantics, authority versus control, lifecycle enabling systems, assumptions, scenario overlays, claim scope, displaced harm, versioning and change triggers.

pedagogical_review.notes: Objectives align with ten distinct examples and five exercises progressing from alternative system framings through human, supplier, security, enabling-system, lifecycle and high-stakes public-context reasoning. The executable checker reinforces metadata consistency without overstating automation.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
